According to Bloomberg's latest report, Apple is less than two weeks away from unveiling a brand-new smart display. The report also further reveals the design details of this highly anticipated smart home hub.

Bloomberg reports that this home hub will feature a 6-inch square screen, with an overall design reminiscent of the classic iMac G4 — back then, the iMac G4 had a dome-shaped base paired with a metal arm supporting the screen, making it an iconic-looking device.

According to Mark Gurman, the device is "about as thick as an iPhone," and features quarter-inch black bezels similar to older iPads. The corners of the body adopt a rounded design, with "no sharp edges at all."

Here are other design details mentioned in the report:

  • The body uses Apple's "standard grey aluminium enclosure," with "rubber material added to the bottom to improve placement stability."
  • It has a USB-C port for power and no built-in battery, so it must be connected to a power source at all times.
  • The base features a "circular metal design with multiple rings of speaker grilles."
  • The screen is connected to the base via a "polished metal arm."
  • Users can tilt the screen forward or backward to adjust the angle.
  • There are no volume buttons or power buttons on the device.
  • There is a FaceTime camera on the front, with no rear camera.

Bloomberg also revealed that there is another version of the home hub "designed for wall mounting." This version is also powered via USB-C, and features a "slim square base below the screen with built-in speakers and microphones." According to reports, the base "sits flush against the wall, mounted below the screen."

To read the full report, head over to Bloomberg. What are your thoughts on Apple's home hub product? Planning to get one (or even several)? Feel free to share your opinions in the comment section.
